'''''Iris latifolia''''', the '''English iris''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> also known as '''''I. xiphiodes''''' and '''''I. anglica''''', is a [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] flowering [[bulb]]ous species of the [[Iris (plant)|Iris]] [[genus]], in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Iridaceae. It is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Pyrenees]] of Southwestern France and Northwestern Spain. It is widely cultivated in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions for its purple flowers which appear in early Summer.

''Iris latifolia'' grows to a height of {{Convert abbreviated|50|cm}}.<ref>[http://www.bulbsociety.org/GALLERY_OF_THE_WORLDS_BULBS/GRAPHICS/Iris/Iris_latifolia/Iris_latifolia.html Iris latifolia<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> 
The plant produces two or three deep purple flowers with yellow marks in the center of the lower petals. Flowers have six [[tepal]]s and are {{Convert abbreviated|12-13|cm}} in diameter. Leaves are stiff and sword-shaped, approximately {{Convert abbreviated|60|cm}} long, and dark green to teal in color. Leaves begin growth in early spring, before the snow has entirely melted. It is a [[bulb]]ous iris, as opposed to a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] iris. The bulb has a thin, dark brown skin and grows {{Convert abbreviated|10-15|cm}} deep in the ground.<ref>{{cite web|title=''Iris latifolia''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=6227|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=23 July 2013}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
